destination.name: Murramarang National Park
destination.tagline: Coastal park of beaches, campgrounds and kangaroos on the sand.
destination.description: Murramarang National Park follows the coast from Long Beach north to Merry Beach, 206 km southwest of Sydney. It is part of the Ulladulla to Merimbula Important Bird Area, recognised for swift parrots. NPWS lists campgrounds and cabins at Depot, Pretty and Pebbly beaches, and kangaroos can be seen on the sand at Pebbly Beach. The 34 km South Coast Walk runs through the park between Ulladulla and Batemans Bay.
whyVisit: Walk the Murramarang South Coast Walk
Camp beside the beach at Pretty Beach

goodToKnow.title: Vehicle fee per day
goodToKnow.detail: Park entry is $8 per vehicle per day; pay machines take cash and cards, but Pretty Beach is card only.

goodToKnow.title: Check the tide
goodToKnow.detail: The South Coast Walk crosses rock platforms that are passable at low tide, so plan its three days around the tide tables.

goodToKnow.title: Stay in the park
goodToKnow.detail: NPWS lists campgrounds and cabins at Depot Beach, Pretty Beach and Pebbly Beach, and the park is open for day visits.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the warm months for beaches and camping on this coast.
